video_title: Doug Christie, Keegan Murray, De’Andre Hunter recap Kings’ loss | NBC Sports California

quotes.speaker: Keegan Murray
quotes.summary_phrase: Keegan Murray on the team's defensive struggles against second-chance points
quotes.excerpt: they were just able to get second chance points and second quarter really hurt us
quotes.quote: I mean it started in the second quarter with their offensive rebounds and at that point they were just able to get second chance points and second quarter really hurt us and at some point in the third quarter hurt us as well and that's when the game got away from us.
quotes.social_post: Keegan Murray says the Kings loss came down to defensive lapses and giving up too many second chance points in the second and third quarters.

structured.context: Keegan Murray discusses the team's defensive struggles regarding second-chance points during their loss.

quotes.speaker: Keegan Murray
quotes.summary_phrase: Keegan Murray on the defensive challenges of guarding Duncan Robinson
quotes.excerpt: you have to be physical with him at the point of the screen
quotes.quote: Duncan Robinson is just a guy that runs off screens. You have to be physical with him at the point of the screen because if he has any daylight he is just going to put it up and he is a really good shooter. Our backside help wasn't great. They hit him a lot when the corner net rolled and he was on the weak side and they hit that skip pass a lot and he was open.
quotes.social_post: Keegan Murray on defending Duncan Robinson: You have to be physical at the point of the screen because if he has any daylight he is going to put it up.

structured.context: Keegan Murray explains the defensive challenges of guarding Duncan Robinson and the team's failure to provide adequate help.

quotes.speaker: Keegan Murray
quotes.summary_phrase: Keegan Murray on the team's defensive rebounding responsibilities
quotes.excerpt: it's the guards that have to come in, rebound and help
quotes.quote: It's a lot on threes. Boston is a team that shoots a lot of threes which means long rebounds and at that point it's the guards that have to come in, rebound and help. It's not on Domantas Sabonis, it's not on Precious Achiuwa, it's not on Dylan Windler, none of those guys because they have to handle the big guy down low and we're getting beat with their guards crashing on offensive rebounds. Our guards just got to get better, we got to be more physical, boxing people out.
quotes.social_post: Keegan Murray says the Kings guards need to do a better job helping on the glass to prevent offensive rebounds.

structured.context: Keegan Murray addresses the team's defensive rebounding responsibilities against Boston.

quotes.speaker: Keegan Murray
quotes.summary_phrase: Keegan Murray on the team's lack of consistency and lapses
quotes.excerpt: our record shows we're not a good team because we have lapses in the middle of games
quotes.quote: Right now our record shows we're not a good team because we have lapses in the middle of games like that. Teams like San Antonio, even with guys out, they're relentless. The guys come off the bench, know what they have to do and they didn't have any lapses. So for us to be at that level, regardless of who plays, you just got to figure it out and there's no excuse for that.
quotes.social_post: Keegan Murray is blunt about the Kings current standing: Right now our record shows we are not a good team because we have lapses in the middle of games.

structured.context: Keegan Murray reflects on the team's lack of consistency and lapses during games.

quotes.speaker: De’Andre Hunter
quotes.summary_phrase: De’Andre Hunter on the team's offensive stagnation against the zone
quotes.excerpt: I think we need more player movement. I think we kind of stalled out
quotes.quote: I think we need more player movement. I think we kind of stalled out, just passed it around the perimeter and you know they kind of forced us to take contested threes.
quotes.social_post: DeAndre Hunter says the Kings offense stalled against the zone because they lacked player movement and settled for contested threes.

structured.context: De’Andre Hunter discusses the team's offensive stagnation while facing a zone defense.

quotes.speaker: De’Andre Hunter
quotes.summary_phrase: De’Andre Hunter on Duncan Robinson's impact on the game
quotes.excerpt: I think Duncan Robinson getting hot, I think that was the second quarter
quotes.quote: I think Duncan Robinson getting hot, I think that was the second quarter, you know he brought them back in the game and I think that gave them life and I think they just carried that throughout the game. They started making shots, they started feeling comfortable and you know we didn't do a good job making them uncomfortable.
quotes.social_post: DeAndre Hunter says Duncan Robinson getting hot in the second quarter gave the opponent life and the Kings failed to make them uncomfortable.

structured.context: De’Andre Hunter analyzes the impact of Duncan Robinson's performance on the game's momentum.

quotes.speaker: De’Andre Hunter
quotes.summary_phrase: De’Andre Hunter on the impact of the opponent's zone defense
quotes.excerpt: I think their zone slowed us down a lot. We couldn't get stops
quotes.quote: I think their zone slowed us down a lot. We couldn't get stops, which stopped us from running in transition, which I think that's when we're at our best. It forced us to play half-court basketball and I think we were just sloppy offensively.
quotes.social_post: DeAndre Hunter says the opponent's zone defense forced the Kings into a half court game and prevented them from running in transition.

structured.context: De’Andre Hunter explains how the opponent's zone defense forced the team into sloppy half-court play.

quotes.speaker: De’Andre Hunter
quotes.summary_phrase: De’Andre Hunter on the importance of defensive rebounding and effort
quotes.excerpt: it's just attention to detail and effort. I think that's the biggest thing
quotes.quote: It's just attention to detail and effort. I think that's the biggest thing. Obviously we're a little undersized with Domantas Sabonis at the five, but I think we still can, you know, defensive rebound a lot better and stop the other team from getting offensive rebounds. So I think that's where we lose a lot of our games at and you know we just have to concentrate and focus on that and probably not worry about other things as much.
quotes.social_post: DeAndre Hunter on the Kings defensive struggles: It is just attention to detail and effort. We have to concentrate and focus on that.

structured.context: De’Andre Hunter emphasizes the need for better defensive rebounding and attention to detail.

quotes.speaker: Doug Christie
quotes.summary_phrase: Doug Christie on the team's lack of energy and discipline
quotes.excerpt: I thought the energy just was low. I talked to them about discipline and consistency
quotes.quote: I thought the energy just was low. I talked to them about discipline and consistency and you know a hot guy, you can't go under. You go under, he hits a shot, he sees it go in and all of a sudden he's in fuego. You got to make sure that you step up, that you turn his water off immediately.
quotes.social_post: Doug Christie on defensive discipline: When a guy gets hot you cannot go under. You have to step up and turn his water off immediately.

structured.context: Doug Christie critiques the team's lack of energy and defensive discipline against hot shooters.

quotes.speaker: Doug Christie
quotes.summary_phrase: Doug Christie on the need for a collective rebounding mentality
quotes.excerpt: it has to be a gang rebound mentality. Everyone has to come back and help out
quotes.quote: This is a second game that we've given up 20 offensive rebounds and it has to be a gang rebound mentality. Everyone has to come back and help out on the backboard. And that doesn't mean turning and looking. I'm sure when I go back and watch this, I'm going to see a lot of that and it's you got to check your guy first, hit him and then pursue the basketball.
quotes.social_post: Doug Christie says the Kings need a gang rebound mentality after giving up 20 offensive rebounds for the second straight game.

structured.context: Doug Christie calls for a collective gang rebounding mentality after the team conceded many offensive rebounds.

quotes.speaker: Doug Christie
quotes.summary_phrase: Doug Christie on the importance of checking your man on shots
quotes.excerpt: when the shot goes up, you have to check your man. That's what you have to do
quotes.quote: When the shot goes up, you have to check your man. That's what you have to do and I'm pretty sure when I go back, I'm going to see a lot of guys just looking and they're just running right at the rim. That is just attention to detail. Is there a little energy in that? Yeah, there is because you got to stay locked in and make sure that you're checking your guy off.
quotes.social_post: Doug Christie on rebounding: When the shot goes up you have to check your man. I am sure when I watch the film I am going to see a lot of guys just looking and running at the rim.

structured.context: Doug Christie stresses the importance of checking opponents on shots to maintain defensive focus.
